text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs to visit Egypt from April 22-25.
- The Union of Christian Democrats and the People's Christian Party (former Latvian Popular Front) announce plans to merge in a few months.
- Public opinion polls name Latvian Independent TV as the country's most popular TV channel with 38 percent of viewing audience.

- The number of unemployed in Latvia's major cities keeps on increasing, according to the statistics committee. The highest level of unemployment is in Rezekne and the Rezekne district, the lowest one is in Ventspils.
- The liquidators of Banka Baltija will begin proceedings against the collapsed bank's off-shore debtors.
- Russian ambassador Alexander Udaltsov handed a letter from president Boris Yeltsin to president Guntis Ulmanis. The topic of the letter was boosting bilateral cooperation.
- Latvia's participation in the trade fair Trans-Russsia 97 was a success.
- Latvia's Socialist Party has decided to back the protests of Latvian farmers against the governmment's agricultural policies.

- Hoyskel & Vennevold, one of Norway's largest food and fish processing groups, acquired a 10 percent stake in Zvejnieks, a Latvian fisheries company. The Norwegian group will invest 240,000 lats by the end of this year.

- Latvian privatisation agency director general Janis Naglis said the shareholders' meeting of Latvian Universal Bank was postponed from April 23 to June 2 and the prospects of the proposed merger between the two banks was unclear.
